title: Vibecoding every city on Earth into tiny playable planets. In Taipei you deliver dumplings and bubble tea 🧋
author: Altruistic_Series258
selftext:
Hey! This is Little Taipei — One of the city I want to turn into a tiny explorable planet.

The idea: build a mini planet for **every city in the world**, each with its own delivery gameplay that fits the city. For Taipei, you deliver dumplings and bubble tea. I started Paris, but I'm focusing on Taipei until it feels truly alive.

I'm trying to respect the real geography as much as possible — landmarks and main roads are placed by actual bearing and distance from Taipei 101, so walking around really *feels* like Taipei: night markets, temples, YouBike stations, the Xiangshan climb, 7-Elevens you can walk into.

The hard part is making each building look like the real thing, and getting the sizes to play well together on a tiny planet. My loop: drop a photo of the actual building, ask the agent to replicate it, walk around the city, adjust.

It's multiplayer by default — I use antics.gg for that, so there are no servers to worry about. Almost all of it is vibecoded: the city is just small, self-contained landmark files + a validated data file of real-world coordinates, which turns out to be a perfect shape for AI agents.

I've open-sourced it hoping to get help making Taipei, but I'd be really delighted to see more cities! https://github.com/craftmygame/little-city/


if you want to play it : https://antics.gg/world/little-taipei

replies.author: dknos_dev
replies.body:
There's lidar/pretty good satellite imagery for my city I get from gov sites and openmaps. Then pointing it at githubs to test out different converting methods, roofer/voxelearth/mroad. Can get the shapes down to a Microsoft FSX level of detail, plus they're destructible/interiors, have fire/collapse physics. Not street level detail, but very walkable, but actually looks good from height.  
  
But really need to replace the generic looking textures building by building which is expensive/time consuming currently. I've done some testing with local generation hyu3d/trellis, but going building by building, finding a picture, removing bg, converting hundreds to thousands, fixing them burns me out.   
  
AI isn't quite there for 3D gaming, but it's getting really close and Kimi3 looks promising in 3D gaming. Makes me want to go downtown and take pictures of every building.
